mainTopic: The number of שבת meals (רבנן vs. רבי חידקא) tested against משניות, rinsing dishes on שבת, and the rewards for the שבת meals.
overview: The amud opens by testing רבי חידקא, who holds that one eats four meals on שבת, against the משנה about saving food from a fire on שבת. Each clause seems to assume only three meals. Each time the גמרא answers that the person already ate a meal. Then רבי יוסי's words in the סיפא, 'always three,' show that the תנא קמא also holds three, so this משנה does not follow רבי חידקא. Next comes the משנה in פאה: someone with food for 14 meals may not take from the קופה. That number fits neither the רבנן (15) nor רבי חידקא (16). The answer for רבי חידקא is rejected because it would make a poor man fast all of Friday. The גמרא concludes that this משנה follows רבי עקיבא: 'Treat your שבת like a weekday rather than depend on other people.' The traveler clause of the same משנה, which gives three שבת meals, can fit רבי חידקא, because the traveler also eats the road meal he brought with him. A ברייתא then teaches when dishes may be rinsed on שבת. The amud ends with אגדה about the great rewards for eating three meals on שבת and for delighting in שבת, and that verse continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Friday night fire: save food for three meals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if a fire breaks out on Friday night, one saves food for three meals. This seems to assume only three שבת meals, against רבי חידקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One may save food for three meals.' Doesn't this mean he has not eaten yet? Then the total is only three meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of a משנה about saving food from a fire on שבת and uses it to challenge רבי חידקא, who says one eats four meals on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On Friday night, before any meal is eaten, you would expect a person to save food for all his remaining שבת meals. The משנה allows only three, so it seems the full total is three, like the רבנן. That would be a problem for רבי חידקא's four.

keyTerms.meaning: We may rescue (save from a fire on שבת)
What, is it not...? (introduces a suggested reading that creates a challenge)
The תנא who holds one must eat four meals on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a quoted משנה. The first words, 'one saves food for three meals,' belong to the case of a fire on Friday night (נפלה דליקה בלילי שבת). This is the background you need for the whole sugya.

phrases.english: one may rescue food for three meals,
phrases.notes: End of the משנה's case of a fire on Friday night.

phrases.english: What, is it not that he has not eaten?!
phrases.notes: If he hasn't eaten yet, three must be the full total.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) of the dispute between the רבנן and רבי חידקא about the number of שבת meals.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חידקא's view that one eats four meals on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On Friday night all the meals are still ahead, yet the משנה allows saving only three. So the total must be three.

steps.title: He already ate the Friday night meal
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה is talking about someone who already ate his Friday night meal, so three of the four meals remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about someone who already ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חידקא by reading the משנה as a case where the person already finished his Friday night meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one meal is already eaten, then four minus one leaves three. The 'three meals' in the משנה can now fit רבי חידקא.

phrases.english: No, it is where he already ate.
phrases.notes: Four total minus one eaten leaves three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the person already ate one meal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה was assumed to speak about someone who has not eaten yet.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks about someone who already ate, so three meals remain under רבי חידקא.

steps.title: Morning fire: save food for two meals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's next clause says that in the morning one saves food for two meals. Again this seems to fit only three meals in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the morning, one saves food for two meals.' Doesn't this mean he hasn't eaten the morning meal yet?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חידקא again, this time from the משנה's case of a fire on שבת morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person has not eaten his morning meal, then two remaining meals means the day has only two meals. Add the night meal and the total is three, like the רבנן.

phrases.english: In the morning, one may rescue food for two meals,
phrases.notes: Next clause of the same משנה.

phrases.english: What, is it not that he has not eaten?
phrases.notes: Then the total would be three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same kind of challenge using the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חידקא's view of four meals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Before the morning meal, only two daytime meals remain, which points to a total of three.

steps.title: He already ate the morning meal
steps.stepSummary: The same answer: the person already ate the morning meal, so two meals remain under רבי חידקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about someone who already ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer again: the person in the משנה already ate the meal for this time of day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Night meal plus morning meal makes two already eaten. Under רבי חידקא, two still remain, which matches the משנה.

phrases.english: No, it is where he already ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 with the same method used in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the morning meal was already eaten.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He had not eaten the morning meal yet.
steps.terutzMaskana: He already ate, so two meals remain out of four.

steps.title: Afternoon fire: save food for one meal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's third clause says that in the afternoon one saves food for one meal. This again seems to point to three meals in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the afternoon, one saves food for one meal.' Doesn't this mean he hasn't eaten yet?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a third challenge from the afternoon (מנחה) clause of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he has not eaten the afternoon meal, then only one meal is left for the rest of שבת. That again totals three.

phrases.english: In the afternoon, one may rescue food for one meal,
What, is it not that he has not eaten?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern of challenge, now from the third clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חידקא's view of four meals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the afternoon only one meal remains, which suggests a total of three.

steps.title: He already ate the afternoon meal
steps.stepSummary: The same answer once more: he already ate the afternoon meal, leaving one more meal under רבי חידקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about someone who already ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the third challenge exactly like the first two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three meals are already eaten, so under רבי חידקא one is left. Each clause of the משנה can be read this way.

phrases.english: No, it is where he already ate!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 the same way as steps 2 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: he already ate.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He had not eaten the afternoon meal.
steps.terutzMaskana: He already ate, so one meal remains out of four.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's 'always three' proves the תנא קמא holds three
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא of the משנה has רבי יוסי saying one always saves food for three meals. So the argument is only about when the fire breaks out, and the תנא קמא also holds three meals in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last part teaches, 'רבי יוסי says: one always saves food for three meals,' this implies the first תנא also holds of three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge from the end of the same משנה, and this one the 'he already ate' answer cannot handle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says 'three' at every time of day. That shows 'three' is the agreed total, and the only question is whether you save for meals already eaten. If the תנא קמא held four, the משנה would show a dispute about the total, but it doesn't.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
The first (anonymous) opinion in a משנה

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
Rabbi Yosei says: always
one may rescue food for three meals —
phrases.notes: At any time of the day.

phrases.english: by implication, the first tanna
holds three!
phrases.notes: Both opinions agree the total is three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the repeated 'he already ate' answers with evidence from the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to fit the משנה with רבי חידקא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's 'always three' shows that three is the shared total in this משנה, so the תנא קמא cannot hold four.

steps.title: This משנה does not follow רבי חידקא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה about the fire does not follow רבי חידקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: our משנה is not like רבי חידקא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on fitting the משנה with רבי חידקא and states that it follows the view of three meals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a refutation of רבי חידקא himself. It only means this משנה reflects the other view. רבי חידקא remains a valid opinion in a מחלוקת.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה of saving food from a fire on שבת assumes three meals, like the רבנן. It does not follow רבי חידקא.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear:
our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Ḥidka.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי חִידְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the force of step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה about the fire follows the view of three שבת meals, not רבי חידקא.

steps.title: The charity משנה's fourteen meals fits neither view
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in פאה says that someone with 14 meals may not take from the communal charity fund. A week has 15 meals according to the רבנן and 16 according to רבי חידקא, so whose view is this?
steps.simpleTranslation: And that which we learned: one who has food for two meals may not take from the תמחוי, and one with food for fourteen may not take from the קופה. Whose view is this? Neither the רבנן nor רבי חידקא. According to the רבנן there are fifteen; according to רבי חידקא, sixteen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question by quoting a משנה about charity, then shows that its number of meals for a week matches neither opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six weekdays at two meals each make 12. Add 3 for שבת and you get 15 (רבנן), or add 4 and you get 16 (רבי חידקא). The משנה's 14 matches neither count.

keyTerms.meaning: And that which we learned in a משנה
Charity plate (daily food handed out to the poor)

phrases.english: And that which we learned:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מְזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת —
phrases.english: one who has food for two meals —
may not take from the charity plate,
food for fourteen —
may not take from the charity fund.

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּי? לָא רַבָּנַן, וְלָא רַבִּי חִידְקָא.
phrases.english: Whose is it? Neither the Rabbis nor Rabbi Ḥidka.
If the Rabbis — they are fifteen.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי חִידְקָא — שֵׁית סְרֵי הָוְיָין!
phrases.english: If Rabbi Ḥidka — they are sixteen!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דִּתְנַן מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מְזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a second משנה that relates to the number of שבת meals.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both the רבנן and רבי חידקא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The weekly meal count implied by the משנה (14) does not match either 15 or 16.

steps.title: Like the רבנן: eat the Saturday night meal on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can follow the רבנן. We tell the poor man to eat the meal he would have eaten on Saturday night during שבת instead, so the week needs only 14 meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it is the רבנן, because we tell him: what you want to eat on מוצאי שבת, eat it on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן could count only 14 meals: one of the שבת meals takes the place of the Saturday night meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The week is counted as if Saturday night's meal is moved into שבת as the third meal. That removes one meal, so 15 becomes 14.

keyTerms.meaning: At the conclusion of שבת (Saturday night)

phrases.english: Actually it is the Rabbis, for we say to him:
what you want to eat at the conclusion of Shabbat,
eat it on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 according to the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recounting the meals: the Saturday night meal is moved into שבת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every meal of the week is counted separately, giving 15.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Saturday night meal is eaten on שבת, so the count is 14.

steps.title: Should we say this משנה follows only the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the charity משנה follows only the רבנן and not רבי חידקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say it is the רבנן, and not רבי חידקא.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the last answer, the גמרא proposes that this משנה must be the רבנן's view alone. This line sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the רבנן can explain the number 14, then this משנה would be another source that goes against רבי חידקא. The גמרא tests whether that is really so.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say (a suggested conclusion, often rejected)

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַבָּנַן הִיא, וְלָא רַבִּי חִידְקָא.
phrases.english: Let us say it is the Rabbis, and not Rabbi Ḥidka.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבָּנַן הִיא וְלָא רַבִּי חִידְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a possible conclusion from the answer in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the charity משנה limited to the רבנן's view?

steps.title: Even רבי חידקא: eat the Friday meal on Friday night
steps.stepSummary: The משנה could follow רבי חידקא too. We tell him to eat his Friday meal on Friday night instead, cutting the count from 16 to 14.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it is רבי חידקא, because we tell him: what you want to eat on ערב שבת, eat it at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 11 by suggesting a similar shift that would let רבי חידקא also arrive at 14 meals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חידקא's week has 16 meals, so two must be removed to reach 14. One is the Saturday night meal, moved into שבת as in step 10. The other is Friday's daytime meal, moved to Friday night. 16 − 2 = 14.

phrases.english: You may even say it is Rabbi Ḥidka,
for we say to him:
what you want to eat on Shabbat eve,
eat it at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 11 that the משנה can only be the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the charity משנה excludes רבי חידקא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A similar moving of meals could make רבי חידקא's count 14 as well.

steps.title: Do we make him fast all of Friday?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: that would mean the poor man eats nothing all day Friday, which is unreasonable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we make him sit fasting the whole day of ערב שבת?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer for רבי חידקא from step 12 as unrealistic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving Friday's daytime meal to Friday night leaves him with no food during the whole of Friday's daytime. We would never require a person to fast all day just to fit the count, so the answer for רבי חידקא fails.

phrases.english: And the whole day of Shabbat eve
do we make him sit fasting?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלֵּי יוֹמָא דְמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא בְּתַעֲנִיתָא מוֹתְבִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי חידקא's count can be reduced by moving Friday's meals to the night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It would force the person to fast all of Friday, which we would never demand.

steps.title: The charity משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: Instead, the charity משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who teaches that it is better to treat שבת like a weekday than to depend on other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, whose view is this? It is רבי עקיבא, who said: Make your שבת like a weekday and do not become dependent on people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the 14-meal question: the משנה follows רבי עקיבא's principle about avoiding charity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that a poor person should eat only two meals on שבת, like any weekday, rather than take charity. Then the week is seven days at two meals each, which is exactly 14. This fits whichever view one holds about the usual number of שבת meals.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who taught avoiding charity even at the cost of שבת honor
Make your שבת like a weekday
And do not become dependent on people

steps.whatToRemember: The 14 meals in the charity משנה follow רבי עקיבא: a poor person eats two meals on שבת, like a weekday, rather than take charity. 7 × 2 = 14.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known principle that a person should cut back on שבת extras rather than become dependent on charity.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying שבת has no special meals. He is giving a rule for a poor person: avoiding charity comes before the extra שבת meal.

phrases.english: Rather, whose view is this —
it is Rabbi Akiva, who said:
Make your Shabbat like a weekday
phrases.notes: Two meals, as on a weekday.

phrases.english: and do not become dependent on people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 12 with a new identification of the משנה's author.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a different תנא (רבי עקיבא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 14 must be explained by moving meals around under the רבנן or רבי חידקא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא: two meals every day including שבת, for a total of 14, rather than taking charity.

steps.title: A second charity משנה about the traveling poor man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a traveling poor man gets at least one loaf. If he sleeps over, he gets lodging. If he stays for שבת, he gets food for three meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about what we learned in a משנה: We do not give a poor man who travels from place to place less than a loaf worth a פונדיון, when wheat sells at four סאה for a סלע. If he sleeps over, we give him what he needs for lodging. If he stays for שבת, we give him food for three meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another משנה about charity. This is a setup line: the next step asks which opinion about שבת meals this משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling comes from the same משנה in פאה (ח:ז) as the תמחוי/קופה ruling discussed before. The גמרא now quotes its earlier clause. The key detail is 'three meals' for שבת. That number will soon be checked against רבי חידקא, who requires four meals on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not give less than (a minimum amount)
A poor man traveling from town to town
A small coin, 1/48 of a סלע

phrases.english: And that which we learned in a Mishnah:
We do not give less to a poor man
who travels from place to place
than a loaf worth a pundeyon,
phrases.notes: The loaf's size is measured by its price.

phrases.english: when wheat sells at four se'a for a sela.
If he sleeps over, we give him lodging needs,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם שָׁבַת — נוֹתְנִין לוֹ מְזוֹן שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת.
phrases.english: and if he stays for Shabbat, we give him food for three meals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second charity משנה that raises the same issue as the first one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A traveling poor man staying for שבת receives food for three meals.

steps.title: Does this משנה follow only the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the traveler משנה matches the רבנן (three שבת meals) and not רבי חידקא (four).
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this משנה follows the רבנן and not רבי חידקא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the 'three meals' in this משנה shows that it disagrees with רבי חידקא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חידקא says one must eat four meals on שבת. A משנה that gives only three seems to follow the רבנן, who require three. The גמרא tests whether that conclusion is really forced.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion that is often rejected)
The תנא who requires four meals on שבת

phrases.english: Shall we say it follows the Rabbis,
and not Rabbi Ḥidka?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבָּנַן הִיא, וְלָא רַבִּי חִידְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a possible conclusion from the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the traveler משנה incompatible with רבי חידקא's four meals?

steps.title: It can follow רבי חידקא: he already has one meal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can follow רבי חידקא. The traveler brought one meal with him, so we tell him to eat it and give him only three more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it follows רבי חידקא. The case is where he has a meal with him, because we tell him: 'Eat the meal you have with you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Even רבי חידקא could agree that the town gives only three meals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He still eats four meals on שבת: three from the town and one he carried in. The משנה only lists what the town must give, not his total for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (introduces a rejection of the suggestion)

phrases.english: Actually, it follows Rabbi Ḥidka:
for example, where there is a meal with him,
for we say to him:
'This meal that you have with you, eat it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the claim that the משנה must follow only the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the conclusion that the משנה cannot fit רבי חידקא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed the three meals were his whole שבת diet. In fact he also eats a meal he brought with him.

steps.title: Will he leave town with nothing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if he eats the meal he brought, he will leave town with no food for the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when he leaves, will he go away empty-handed?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Eating his own meal would leave the traveler with nothing for his journey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The traveler carried that meal for his trip. If he uses it up on שבת, he walks out on Sunday with no food. It seems unreasonable that the charity rules would set things up this way.

phrases.english: And when he goes, will he go empty-handed?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the traveler eats the meal he brought.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating his travel meal leaves him with nothing when he departs. That is an unreasonable result.

steps.title: We send him off with a meal for the road
steps.stepSummary: The town gives him a meal to take with him when he leaves, so he is never left empty-handed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We send him off with a meal to take along.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that every town sends the traveler off with a meal for the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each town gives him a meal for the journey. He eats that meal on שבת in the next town, and when he leaves, that town gives him a new one. So he always arrives with one meal and always leaves with one meal.
steps.whatToRemember: The traveler משנה can follow רבי חידקא. The town gives three שבת meals, and he eats a fourth: the road meal the previous town gave him. When he leaves, the town gives him a new road meal.

phrases.english: We send him off with a meal to take along.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge and keeps the משנה in line with רבי חידקא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a practical detail: the town gives a meal for the road when he departs.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating his carried meal would leave him with no food when he leaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is always given a new road meal when he departs, so the four-meal reading works.

steps.title: What are 'lodging needs'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by פרנסת לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'lodging needs'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה to explain the meaning of one of its terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says to give 'lodging needs' to a traveler who sleeps over, but it does not say what that includes. The גמרא wants a concrete definition.

phrases.english: What is 'lodging needs'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meals issue to explaining another phrase in the same משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical meaning of פרנסת לינה.

steps.title: A bed and cushions
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that lodging needs means a bed and cushions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A bed and cushions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defines the term: the town provides a bed and bedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lodging needs means the items needed for sleeping, a bed and cushions. It is not more food, since the loaf he was given already covers his night meal.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who defines the term

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
A bed and cushions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: פּוּרְיָא וּבֵי סַדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lodging needs means a bed and cushions.

steps.title: Rinsing bowls between שבת meals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that bowls may be rinsed on שבת only if they will be used again at a later שבת meal. After the afternoon meal, they may no longer be rinsed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Bowls one ate from at night may be rinsed to eat from them in the morning. Bowls from the morning may be rinsed for the midday meal. Bowls from midday may be rinsed for the afternoon meal. From the afternoon meal onward, one may not rinse them anymore.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about washing dishes on שבת. It connects to the theme of the שבת meals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rinsing is allowed only when the bowls are needed for another meal on שבת itself. After the last meal there is no more use for them on שבת. Rinsing them then would be preparing on שבת for a weekday, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The afternoon (here, the last meal of שבת)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not forbid washing dishes on שבת in general. It forbids only washing that serves a weekday, after the last שבת meal.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Bowls from which one ate in the evening:
he may rinse them to eat from them in the morning.
Those from the morning: he may rinse them to eat from them at midday.
Those from midday: he may rinse them to eat from them in the afternoon.
From the afternoon onward,
he no longer rinses them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קְעָרוֹת שֶׁאָכַל בָּהֶן עַרְבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the שבת meals: rinsing dishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bowls may be rinsed on שבת only for use at a later שבת meal. After the afternoon meal, rinsing is not allowed.

steps.title: Drinking vessels may be rinsed all day
steps.stepSummary: Cups, ladles and flasks may be rinsed all day, because there is no fixed time for drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: But cups, ladles and flasks may be rinsed all day long, because there is no fixed time for drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds an exception for drinking vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person might want a drink at any moment on שבת, even after the last meal. So rinsing a cup is always considered preparing for שבת, not for the weekday.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no fixed time for drinking

phrases.english: But cups, ladles and flasks:
he may keep rinsing them all day long,
because there is no fixed time for drinking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with an exception to the bowls rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking vessels may be rinsed all day, since one may drink at any time on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Food bowls may be rinsed only for another שבת meal. Cups may be rinsed all day, because drinking has no fixed time.

steps.title: Three שבת meals save from three punishments
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא teaches that whoever eats three meals on שבת is saved from the birth pangs of משיח, the judgment of גיהנם, and the war of גוג ומגוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said it in the name of בר קפרא: Whoever keeps the three meals of שבת is saved from three troubles: the birth pangs of משיח, the judgment of גיהנם, and the war of גוג ומגוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to אגדה and brings a teaching about the great reward for eating three meals on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three meals match three rescues. The next step will show where each of the three rescues comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The birth pangs (hard times) before משיח comes
The war of גוג ומגוג at the end of days

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
in the name of bar Kappara:
Whoever fulfills three meals on Shabbat
is saved from three punishments:
from the birth pangs of Messiah,
and from the judgment of Gehenna,
and from the war of Gog and Magog.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the laws of the שבת meals to their spiritual reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating three meals on שבת saves a person from three future punishments.

steps.title: The word 'day' links שבת to each rescue
steps.stepSummary: Each of the three rescues is learned from the word 'יום' (day). That word appears in the שבת verse and also in a verse about each of the three troubles.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the birth pangs of משיח: it says 'day' here, and it says there: 'Behold, I send you אליהו the prophet before the coming of the day.' From the judgment of גיהנם: it says 'day' here, and it says there: 'That day is a day of wrath.' From the war of גוג ומגוג: it says 'day' here, and it says there: 'On the day that גוג comes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves each of the three rescues from a shared word, 'יום' (day).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about the מן says 'today' three times, and this is the source for three שבת meals. Each of the three troubles is also called a 'day' in its own verse. The shared word ties keeping the שבת 'day' to being saved on each of those 'days.'

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here, and it is written there (a word link between verses)
אליהו the prophet, who comes before משיח

steps.confusionAlert: 'Here' (הכא) means the שבת verse about the מן: 'Eat it today' (שמות טז:כה). The גמרא does not quote that verse, but it is the one being referred to.

phrases.english: From the birth pangs of Messiah:
it is written here 'day',
and it is written there:
'Behold, I am sending you
Elijah the prophet
before the coming of the day, etc.'
From the judgment of Gehenna:
it is written here 'day',
and it is written there:
'That day is a day of wrath.'
From the war of Gog and Magog:
it is written here 'day',
and it is written there:
'On the day that Gog comes.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for each of the three rescues named in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That the three שבת meals save from the three punishments.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word 'יום' in the שבת verse and in מלאכי, צפניה and יחזקאל.

steps.title: Delighting in שבת earns a boundless inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי יוסי, teaches that whoever delights in שבת receives an inheritance without borders. The proof verse comes from ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי: Whoever delights in שבת is given an inheritance without borders, as it says: 'Then you will delight in ה', and I will make you ride on the heights of the earth, and I will feed you…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אגדה teaching about the reward for enjoying שבת. The verse continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a second reward: an inheritance with no boundaries. The verse quoted here ties delighting in שבת to that reward. The end of the verse, which shows what makes the inheritance 'boundless,' comes in the next part of the text.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
Whoever delights in the Shabbat
is given an inheritance without borders,
as it is stated:
'Then you will delight in the Lord,
and I will make you ride on the heights of the earth,
and I will feed you…'
phrases.notes: The verse continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another reward for honoring שבת, continuing the אגדה theme.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever delights in שבת receives a boundless inheritance.
